name: Modern man-to-man
scopeNote: Man-marking over most of the pitch combined with a high or aggressive press and a back three, 2016 to today. Gasperini's Atalanta (2016-2025, Europa League 2024) is the core (Il Foglio: 'marcatura individuale a tutto campo'; Il Post 2017 'marcandoli a uomo a tutto campo'), carried to Roma 2025/26. Tudor (Verona 2021/22, Marseille 2022/23, Juventus 2025) is a derivative: tier A/B sources only support man-orientated marking in defensive transitions with a mid-block press (Verona; The Analyst) and 'marquage individuel' at Marseille (Rothen, a pundit); no verified man-marking source for Juventus. Distinct from bielsismo (that file is 1990-2020, Bielsa's own lineage with a spare centre-back and 3-3-1-3); here the exemplars are Gasperini's 3-4-2-1/3-4-3 five-at-the-back version. Start is year-month only (Gasperini's Atalanta start in June 2016 per Il Foglio 'a Bergamo dal 2016' / TFT pre-contract; exact day not checked). Stricter label: 'man-oriented' rather than pure man-to-man, since Atalanta mix zonal concepts (Crooks).
openQuestions: Ids: no catalog entry exists for Gasperini, Tudor or Atalanta. Proposed: manager 'gian-piero-gasperini', manager 'igor-tudor', team 'atalanta-2016-25' (or atalanta-2016-24, to Europa League). Roma 2025/26 could be a team entry 'roma-2025-26'.

Tudor as exemplar is weakly supported: The Analyst says his man-orientation was NOT pitch-wide at Verona (mid-block); Il Foglio only lists him among those inspired by the Gasperini model. Consider Ivan Juric (Gasperini's former pupil, These Football Times) as a closer second exemplar.
Gasperini's end at Atalanta and Roma appointment (2025-06) and the Roma 2025/26 season rest on Il Foglio/Chiesa di Totti/Corriere dello Sport; exact leaving date not verified.
Search-summary only (not verified): UEFA Europa League final analysis (man-for-man marking vs Leverkusen) was not-accessible; Tudor's Juventus man-marking not found in any readable source.

Gap pass search on Tudor/Verona found no explicit Gasperini link in a 2021/22 source; a 'man-marking all over the pitch' Tudor claim at Marseille comes only from Rothen's quote and an unread match report.
